subject: Post-call: FinLytics pricing & volume quick qualification
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-20T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: FinLytics pricing & volume quick qualification

Team — quick recap from today

Summary of call (FinLytics / Tom Reynolds):
- Use case: realtime risk-scoring + analytics pipeline (low-latency chat + batch embeddings for nightly re-index).
- Expected initial ramp: 30M tokens/month with business-case spike up to ~80M tokens/month during batch windows. Steady-state target: 50M+/month if early tests go well.
- Primary asks: target $/1M tokens they'd be comfortable with ($200–$300 range mentioned on the call), SLA (p99 latency target ~150ms for chat), and a comparison vs OpenAI/Anthropic TCO.

Notes / qualification:
- They are price-sensitive and want a clear per-1M token benchmark.
- Procurement wants a 12-month committed pricing option if we can hit their target rates.
- Tech: they will run mixed workloads (chat + embeddings). Latency is a gating factor for chat; embeddings can be offloaded to cheaper quantized runs.

Attachments: call-recording.mp3 (30m), calculation-sheet.xlsx (ballpark math)

Suggested immediate next steps:
1) Send Tom a short benchmarking email that compares Redwoods hosted/dedicated $/1M to OpenAI/Anthropic and a simple spend table for the 30M / 50M / 80M buckets.
2) Propose two price points: Hosted (no commit) and Dedicated (12-month commit) with volume break incentives.
3) Loop in pricing (Marissa) and growth discounts (Vivek) to validate margins before customer-facing doc.

I'll draft the outbound; Marissa/Vivek please confirm if we can flex below $300/1M on Dedicated for 12mo commit.

— Karthik

From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@finlytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-21T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: FinLytics pricing & volume quick qualification

Karthik — thanks for the recap and for jumping on this quickly. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The volumes are our current internal estimate: 30M/mo during POC with the potential to scale to 50–80M/mo within 3–6 months if the accuracy and latency look good. Spikes will be concentrated during end-of-day batch jobs (embeddings) and intraday for risk alerts (chat).
- Our procurement target is efficiency around $200–$300 per 1M tokens; we'd consider a 12-month commit if the committed price lines up (and if there are clear SLOs).
- Can you share a short benchmarking note that compares what we'd actually pay to OpenAI/Anthropic/open-model hosts for similar workloads — we need a simple delta that our Finance team can read (expected spend per month at 30M/50M/80M).
- Also need confirmation of latency guarantees for chat and what happens if we exceed the committed volume (overage pricing).

Happy to jump on a short follow-up call next week once you send details.

Thanks,
Tom
Director of Data Products
FinLytics

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@finlytics.com>, procurement@finlytics.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-21T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: FinLytics pricing & volume quick qualification

Tom — thanks, attaching a short benchmarking note and a draft pricing sketch (attached: redwood-pricing-draft.pdf). Key points up front:

Benchmarks (ballpark $/1M tokens, public host list):
- OpenAI (GPT-family): ~ $1,200–$1,600 / 1M tokens for higher-capability endpoints (charged at per-1k token rates translated to 1M basis).
- Anthropic: ~ $900–$1,300 / 1M tokens depending on model/throughput tier.
- Open-model hosts / self-hosted + infra (managed): broad range, typically $300–$800 / 1M depending on committed infra, quantization, and ops overhead.

Our preliminary (Redwood) pricing sketch for FinLytics:
- Hosted (no commit): $425 / 1M tokens — includes managed runtime, standard rate limits, built-in caching and observed SLOs.
- Dedicated (12-month commit, 50M+/mo target): $275 / 1M tokens — dedicated GPU pools, tail-latency optimization, priority routing, and custom batching/caching profiles.
- Overage: 10% premium above committed unit price, with automatic burst protections to avoid downtime.

Estimated monthly spend (illustrative):
- 30M/mo: Hosted = $12,750; Dedicated (if eligible) = $8,250
- 50M/mo: Hosted = $21,250; Dedicated = $13,750
- 80M/mo: Hosted = $34,000; Dedicated = $22,000

How we compare:
- Compared to OpenAI/Anthropic list prices, Redwood Dedicated at scale materially reduces unit cost, and our cost advantage vs OpenAI increases with committed volumes due to routing & quantization options.
- Open-model hosts can be cheaper at scale but often require either self-managing ops or lower reliability SLAs; Redwood Dedicated is positioned to hit a middle-ground: high reliability + lower unit cost than public hosted alternatives.

Next steps I propose:
1) If the above is directionally useful, we'll finalize a one-page commercial offer (commit tiers + overage terms + SLOs) for your procurement.
2) Marissa/Vivek — please confirm margin comfort on Dedicated $275/1M for a 12mo commit at 50M+/mo; if not, propose a range we can present.
3) Tech follow-up: set a short call between our infra lead and your platform engineer to validate latency and KV-cache behavior.

I'm available this week for a 20–30m call to walk through the attached note.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-22T08:55:00-07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Approval request — FinLytics draft pricing (FIN-2026-041)

Folks — forwarding Tom's confirmation (below) and our draft sketch. Need quick approvals so we can send a formal offer tomorrow.

Quoted outbound (proposed): Dedicated: $275 / 1M tokens (12-month commit, target 50M+/mo)
Hosted: $425 / 1M tokens (no commit)
Overage: +10% on unit price; auto-burst to avoid service interruption.

Why this is needed:
- Prospect target is $200–$300 / 1M; our Dedicated price hits the upper bound of that band.
- If we go lower, margin compression is material unless we lock a 12mo commit + prepay. Need pricing team to confirm break-even vs infra cost assumptions in calculation-sheet.xlsx.

Asks: 
1) Marissa — confirm whether we can accept $275 / 1M on a 12mo commit with a prepay or monthly billing (which helps margin). If not, proposed counter-range?
2) Vivek — any quick partner/market discounts we should layer (e.g., startup credits, first-3-months-free) to help close without dropping unit price?
3) Grace — escalation authority: can we approve up to $250 / 1M for strategic customers in exchange for 24mo commit?

Quoted customer email (excerpt):
> "Our procurement target is efficiency around $200–$300 per 1M tokens; we'd consider a 12-month commit if the committed price lines up (and if there are clear SLOs)."

I'll hold on sending the formal PDF until we have alignment — want to avoid back-and-forth with procurement.

— Karthik
